$comment: TASK-1055 — additions to the model-residency contracts, PINNED by the orchestrator before the lanes branched (wave 0). Additive to model-residency-agent.fixture.json / -admin / -catalogue: every TASK-1005/1051 shape stays valid. Lanes: L-KERNEL (packages/py-runtime-models), L-STT, L-NLP, L-LMS-AGENT (infrastructure/docker/lmstudio/agent), L-GATEWAY, L-CONSOLE, L-DEPLOY.

deviceIds.$comment: Two vocabularies, one mapping. Agents speak `cuda:<n>` = the n-th GPU the PROCESS sees with CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID (deployment sets it on stt, stt-worker, nlp, lmstudio). The gateway/console speak the catalogue id `gpu<n>` = DCGM's `gpu` label (PCI order on this node). Mapping rule in the gateway: match the agent device's `uuid` against DCGM's `UUID` label; fall back to `cuda:<n>` -> `gpu<n>` only when the agent reports no uuid. `multi` (LM Studio split per profile) and `cpu` pass through unchanged.

python.$comment: Residency agent v2 (stt, nlp — and the LM Studio agent speaks the SAME snake_case shapes). New fields are optional; an absent `device` keeps TASK-1005 behaviour.
python.$reportNotes: `devices[]` lists EVERY GPU the process sees (not only the ones holding a model) — the gateway ranks them. `process_bytes` = what this process holds on the card (torch.cuda.memory_reserved for torch services; null when unknowable). The same model loaded on two devices is TWO entries, distinguished by `device`. `bytes_source`: `measured` = parameter+buffer bytes (torch) or a clean, serialised per-device delta; `estimated` = file size / polluted delta; `unknown`.

error.message: no room to load X on cuda:0: ...

python.unloadSemantics: An unload MUST return the memory to the driver before it answers: drop every reference (cache entry, service shutdown(), weight registry), gc, then `release_accelerator_memory(device)` (torch empty_cache on that device). The next load's measurement starts from a clean baseline.

lmStudioAgent.$comment: L-LMS-AGENT: a sidecar container in the hope-lmstudio pod, Node, listening on :8869, talking to the daemon over loopback ws://127.0.0.1:1234 with the SDK `loadModel` channel (reusing infrastructure/docker/lmstudio/loader/kvconfig.mjs). Routes and snake_case bodies are the `python` block's, prefixed /internal/residency. Auth: `X-Service-Token` = INTERNAL_ACCESS_TOKEN (constant-time compare; empty = dev bypass, as the python services). The gateway reaches it at env LMSTUDIO_AGENT_URL (k8s: http://hope-lmstudio:8869). GET /health answers 200 when the daemon greets — this is what the pod's readiness becomes (OD-6).
lmStudioAgent.$loadNotes: `model_ref` is the catalogue ref (AiModel.wireModelId, the bare name). The AGENT resolves the engine key with the boot loader's `selectModelKey` rules (exact key, else the unique `<ref>@<quant>`, never `@?`). `load_spec` is the model's resolved serving profile, built by the gateway with the SAME resolution as the boot plan (effective-config lmStudioServing.preload entry). `device`: `cuda:<n>` overrides gpu_split to `{priorityOrder, priority:[n], disabled_gpus:[all others]}`; absent = the profile's gpu_split; the gateway sends `multi` as an absent device + profile split `evenly` when the admin picks 'split across cards'. The agent loads with `identifier`, verifies the applied config by read-back (strict), and answers like the python agent. An instance with that identifier already loaded = `already_loaded`.
lmStudioAgent.$reportNotes: `device` = `cuda:<n>` when the instance sits on one card, `multi` when split. `device_bytes` = per-card delta measured by nvidia-smi around the agent's OWN serialised load (one load at a time per daemon); instances loaded before the agent started (boot plan) report `bytes_source: estimated` with the file size split by the configured split. Instances in the daemon that no `identifier` names (JIT loads) are reported with model_ref = their engine key.

loadPreviewResponseAdditions.suggestionReason: GPU 1 has 10.0 GB free above headroom; GPU 0 is 1.7 GB short.

gateway.$suggestionRule: (Revised after review R1-F1.) Candidates = every device the service can place on (stt/nlp: the GPUs their agent reports; lm-studio: every GPU plus `multi`). Order: the TARGET the load takes with no device (on a replace: where the instance is now; else `_metadata.residency.defaultDevice`; else the serving profile; else the service default) leads whenever it fits; then fitting single cards (most `remainingBytes` -> fewer `livePathModels` -> lower index); `multi` only when no single card fits and the split does (judged PER CARD: each card must hold its share of an even/custom split); none fits -> single cards first, smallest `shortfallBytes`. `exceedsDevice` = need (or a card's share) > that card's freeBytes, ignoring headroom.

body.message: GPU 0 cannot hold … (short 1.7 GB). GPU 1 can.

OVER_BUDGET.note: Un-forced load over the chosen device's budget. `force: true` + reason proceeds unless EXCEEDS_DEVICE.

body.message: …needs more than GPU 0 has free at all; a forced load would OOM its card-mates

EXCEEDS_DEVICE.note: OD-5 hard refusal, even with force.

reviewRefusals.$comment: Added by the review fix wave (R2-F6, R2-F7, R2-F8).

body.message: a forced over-budget load is never made the default

reviewRefusals.LIVE_PATH_REASON_REQUIRED_on_replace: A `load` with `replace: true` of a live-path model answers the same 409 LIVE_PATH_REASON_REQUIRED body as unload.
reviewRefusals.auditAction: makeDefault writes emit `model-residency.default-device {service, aiModelId, modelRef, device, previousDevice[, gpuSplit, previousGpuSplit]}` only after the load succeeds (or at once when already loaded on that device).
reviewRefusals.metadata: `AiModel._metadata.residency.observedContextLength` = the context the observed footprint was measured at (scales the need of a larger-context load).

lmStudioAgentExtras.load_spec.expected_bytes: optional positive int — the agent refuses 503 INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY {device, needed_bytes, free_bytes} when a target card's share exceeds nvidia-smi free

body.message: Medical NER is on the live consultation path; give a reason to unload it

LIVE_PATH_REASON_REQUIRED.note: OD-2: a live-path model (implicit or PINNED policy) may be unloaded with a non-empty reason, audited. No policy row is created or changed by an unload.

gateway.makeDefault: OD-4: `makeDefault: true` (requires `device`) writes `AiModel._metadata.residency.defaultDevice = <gpuN|multi|cpu>` with OCC; for lm-studio it ALSO writes `_metadata.serving.gpuSplit` (priorityOrder [n] / evenly) so the boot plan follows. A load without `device` uses `defaultDevice`, else the service default.
gateway.measurementRule: A new measurement replaces `AiModel.observedMemoryMb` only when it is `measured` AND >= 50 % of the stored value (else it is logged at warn and the stored value kept). One unattributed formula: device.usedBytes - sum(per-device bytes of every instance on it), shared by catalogue and preview.

wave3.$comment: TASK-1055 wave 3 (README §10) — every agent kind loads on request OR by the platform admin; loading never needs an agent. Frozen before the lanes start; lanes build against it in parallel.

effectiveConfig.$comment: GET /internal/effective-config?service=lmstudio → lmStudioServing gains `profiles`: one entry per ENABLED SYSTEM lm-studio AiModel row (same shape and resolver as `preload`, lmStudioPreloadEntryFor). `preload` is unchanged (still the boot list).

ensure.$comment: LM Studio agent, port 8869, X-Service-Token = INTERNAL_ACCESS_TOKEN (same rule as every /internal route). Matches a resident instance by identifier OR model key. Loads with the cached profile through the SAME single-flight path as POST /internal/residency/load (a concurrent console load and ensure produce ONE instance). Profiles come from the agent's periodic plan refresh; never a request-time gateway call.

body.message: no serving profile for 'x' in the LM Studio plan

textCaller.$comment: apps/text lmstudio provider: before EVERY request to an LM Studio model, POST ensure {model_ref: <the request's model id>}. 200 → proceed. 503 LOAD_FAILED → fail the request (503, cause kept). Unreachable / timeout / 404 MODEL_UNKNOWN / 401 → log `text.lmstudio.ensure_skipped` (warning) and proceed (LM Studio JIT, today's behaviour). Agent URL: env `TEXT_LMSTUDIO_AGENT_URL` (bootstrap transport address; empty = feature off, proceed). Ensure timeout: the request's own timeout budget (a cold load can take minutes).

sttModelOnly.$comment: New stt residency load spec: {"model": <one ResolvedAsrSpec model object, exactly the wire shape of models.<role>>}. `_plan` requires model.slug == model_ref, builds the AiModelConfig with the same to_ai_model_config, loads via get_model_cache(device).get_or_load (slug key — sessions reuse it). Any role: asr | vad | denoise | embedding (diarization embedding) | punctuation | endpointing. The {"resolved_spec"} shape stays accepted. The gateway ALWAYS sends the model-only shape from the console (W3-2), built from the AiModel row with the same projection buildResolvedAsrSpec uses for that role.

refusals.INVALID_LOAD_SPEC: model.slug != model_ref, or the object fails the spec model's validation (extra=forbid)
refusals.DEVICE_UNAVAILABLE: device names a card this pod cannot place on

ttsResidency.$comment: apps/tts mounts the shared residency router at /internal/residency (X-Service-Token = INTERNAL_ACCESS_TOKEN; tenant header rule as stt/nlp). Resident set = the registered LOCAL providers' ModelCache entries (Kokoro, Indic Parler, Indic F5); remote engines (azure, sarvam) never appear. model_ref = the AiModel slug; cache = `tts_<engine>`; device = `cpu`. Unload evicts the provider's cache entry (the provider stays registered; the next synth request reloads it — on-request load is unchanged). Policy (ttl) follows the shared kernel.
ttsResidency.engineFromRow: ttsEngineProvider(row) in packages/applications/src/services/agent/tts-spec.ts (slug with '-' → '_' unless the row names its engine) — the SAME name apps/tts registers the provider under

refusals.MODEL_UNKNOWN: no registered local provider named load_spec.engine (or a remote engine)

ttsResidency.$amendment: 2026-10-09 (after lane W3-TTS): a COLD console load must work on a fresh pod, so load_spec also carries `model` — the TtsSpecModel wire object (exactly ResolvedTtsCandidate.model, built by the gateway from the AiModel row with tts-spec.ts toSpecModel/the same projection). The tts agent builds the engine through the SAME builder and the SAME engine-cache key the synth request path uses, so the next request reuses that instance (never a second copy); if no engine is built yet and `model` is absent → MODEL_UNKNOWN as before.

gateway.$comment: RESIDENCY_CONTROLLED_SERVICES gains 'tts' (agent at TTS_URL). Catalogue: a 'Text-to-speech' section (runsOn cpu) listing self-hosted tts rows (kokoro / indic-parler / indic-f5), cloud rows `remote`. stt stage rows (VAD / denoise / diarization / embedding) are loadable (loadBlockedReason no longer refuses them); built-in rows stay `builtin`. Console labels the tts service 'Text-to-speech'.
